group.title: Holidays
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: To put clothes and things into a bag for a trip.
examples: I need to {pack} my suitcase tonight.
wrong: I packed my bag by taking everything out of it.

words.meaning: The bags and cases you take on a trip.
examples: Please collect your {baggage} after the flight.
wrong: Baggage is the ticket you show to the driver.

words.meaning: The desk near the door of a hotel where guests are welcomed.
examples: Leave your key at {reception} when you go out.
wrong: We slept in the reception of our room every night.

words.meaning: A room you pay to sleep in at a hotel.
examples: Our {hotel room} has two beds and a big window.
wrong: We cooked dinner for fifty people in our small hotel room.

words.meaning: An arrangement to have a room, seat or table kept for you.
examples: I made a {booking} for three nights.
wrong: We made a booking, so there was no room for us.

words.meaning: A plastic card that opens your hotel room door.
examples: Put the {key card} in the slot to open the door.
wrong: I paid for lunch with my hotel key card from the bank.

words.meaning: What you can see from a place, for example from a window.
examples: Our room has a lovely {view} of the mountains.
wrong: The room had a beautiful view because it had no windows.

words.meaning: A long warm bag that you sleep inside, for example in a tent.
examples: Bring a {sleeping bag} because the nights are cold.
wrong: He carried water to the camp in his sleeping bag.

words.meaning: A bag that you carry on your back.
examples: She carried her water and map in her {backpack}.
wrong: He wore his backpack on his head like a hat.

words.meaning: A small, simple hotel, often in a family home.
examples: We stayed in a quiet {guesthouse} near the harbor.
wrong: The guesthouse is a huge hotel with a thousand rooms.

words.meaning: A fire that people make outside when they are camping.
examples: We sang songs around the {campfire}.
wrong: We lit a campfire in the hotel bathroom.

words.meaning: A visit around a place to see the interesting parts.
examples: We took a bus {tour} of the city.
wrong: The tour stayed in one room and saw nothing.

words.meaning: A place on the coast where boats stay safe from the sea.
examples: The fishing boats came back to the {harbor}.
wrong: The harbor is in the desert, far from any water.

words.meaning: In or to a foreign country.
examples: We go {abroad} every summer, usually to Spain.
wrong: She went abroad to the shop on her street.

words.meaning: Late; happening later than planned.
examples: Our flight was {delayed} by two hours.
wrong: The train was delayed, so it left early.

words.meaning: To swim with your face in the water, breathing through a tube.
examples: We {snorkeled} and saw colorful fish.
wrong: We snorkeled on the dry sand all afternoon.

words.meaning: A time when you don’t work or study and often travel.
examples: We’re going to the beach on {vacation}.
wrong: I’m on vacation, so I have to go to the office all week.

words.meaning: A place in the mountains where people go to ski.
examples: The {ski resort} has lots of snow this year.
wrong: We went to a ski resort on a hot, flat beach.

words.meaning: A person whose job is to show visitors around a place.
examples: Our {guide} told us about the old church.
wrong: The guide got lost and asked us the way.

words.meaning: To use a camera or phone to make a picture.
examples: Can you {take a photo} of us by the lake?
wrong: I took a photo by closing my eyes and singing.

words.meaning: A place by the sea where people go on holiday.
examples: We spent a week at the {seaside}.
wrong: The seaside is far from any water.

words.meaning: A car that you pay to use for a short time.
examples: We picked up a {rental car} at the airport.
wrong: I bought a rental car, so it’s mine forever.

words.meaning: To say that something you planned will not happen.
examples: We had to {cancel} our trip because of the storm.
wrong: They canceled the flight, so it left on time.

words.meaning: To come down from the air onto the ground.
examples: The plane {landed} at six in the morning.
wrong: The plane landed and flew high above the clouds.

words.meaning: The darker color your skin gets after being in the sun.
examples: She came back from the beach with a nice {tan}.
wrong: He got a tan by staying inside all summer.

words.meaning: A small cabin that hangs from a wire and carries people up a mountain.
examples: We took the {cable car} to the top of the mountain.
wrong: The cable car drove us along the highway.

words.meaning: A small flying insect that bites people.
examples: A {mosquito} bit me on the arm last night.
wrong: The mosquito barked at the mailman.

words.meaning: Light open shoes held on by a strap between your toes.
examples: I wear {flip-flops} at the beach.
wrong: He wore his flip-flops to climb the snowy mountain.

words.meaning: Open shoes with straps, worn in warm weather.
examples: It’s hot, so I’m wearing {sandals}.
wrong: She wore her sandals on her hands to keep warm.

words.meaning: Things you use to wash and clean yourself, like soap.
examples: I keep my {toiletries} in a small bag.
wrong: I packed my toiletries: two books and a pen.

words.meaning: The hard outside part of a small sea animal, found on beaches.
examples: The children collected {shells} on the beach.
wrong: We picked shells from the apple tree.

words.meaning: A small object that lets your plug fit a foreign socket.
examples: Bring an {adapter} for your phone charger.
wrong: I used an adapter to open the bottle.

words.meaning: A small hotel or house where you get a room and a morning meal.
examples: We stayed at a {bed and breakfast} by the sea.
wrong: The bed and breakfast gave us no bed and no food.

words.meaning: The large area inside the front door of a hotel.
examples: Let’s meet in the hotel {lobby} at eight.
wrong: We had a bath in the hotel lobby.

words.meaning: A person who is on a trip or who travels often.
examples: The hostel was full of young {travelers}.
wrong: She is a traveler because she has never left her town.

words.meaning: A large old building with thick walls, built to protect people.
examples: We visited a {castle} on the hill.
wrong: The castle is a small tent made of paper.

words.meaning: A folding chair you sit or lie on at the beach.
examples: Dad slept in a {deck chair} by the pool.
wrong: I washed the dishes in the deck chair.

words.meaning: What you can see of the ocean from a window or balcony.
examples: We paid more for a room with a {sea view}.
wrong: Our room had a sea view, so we could only see a parking lot.

words.meaning: A person who looks after passengers on a plane.
examples: The {flight attendant} brought us drinks.
wrong: The flight attendant drove the bus to the city.

words.meaning: To ride on the waves of the sea standing on a board.
examples: They {surf} every morning when the waves are big.
wrong: He surfed down the snowy mountain on skis.
